blogs.title: When the Triad is Missing: Recognizing Telomere Biology Disorders in Adults
blogs.description: Many clinicians only associate Telomere Biology Disorders (TBDs) with the classic mucocutaneous triad of Dyskeratosis Congenita. This post explores how TBDs can present as 'idiopathic' pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic cirrhosis, or isolated bone marrow failure in young adults, and why clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for premature aging features (like greying hair or knuckle hyperpigmentation) in cases of multisystem organ failure.

blogs.title: The Anchor Bias of Nutritional Deficiencies: When 'Corrected' Labs Aren't the End of the Story
blogs.description: In this case, severe vitamin B12 deficiency provided an initial explanation for the patient's pancytopenia and fatigue. However, the persistence of systemic symptoms despite nutritional correction is a major clinical 'red flag.' We discuss how to avoid diagnostic anchoring and recognize when a nutritional deficiency is a secondary manifestation of a deeper, underlying genetic pathology.

blogs.title: Decoding the Smear: Distinguishing Ineffective Erythropoiesis from Peripheral Destruction
blogs.description: A laboratory-focused deep dive into the peripheral smear findings of dimorphic erythrocytes, basophilic stippling, and Cabot rings. We will discuss how to interpret a positive Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) in the context of a low reticulocyte count, helping clinicians differentiate between immune-mediated hemolysis and the ineffective erythropoiesis characteristic of marrow failure syndromes.

blogs.title: Expanding the PARN Phenotype: From Pulmonary Fibrosis to Hepatic Cirrhosis
blogs.description: While monoallelic PARN mutations are increasingly recognized in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), this case highlights an expanding clinical spectrum that includes hepatic fibrosis and bone marrow failure. We will review the current literature on PARN-associated TBDs and discuss the importance of considering these mutations in patients with unexplained, progressive fibrotic liver disease.

blogs.title: Clinical Correlation vs. Genetic Certainty: Managing the 'Variant of Uncertain Significance'
blogs.description: Genetic testing often returns a 'Variant of Uncertain Significance' (VUS), which can be frustrating for clinicians seeking a definitive diagnosis. This post discusses the management of patients who have a high clinical correlation with a genetic variant that hasn't been fully validated, focusing on how to guide surveillance, genetic counseling, and long-term management in the face of diagnostic ambiguity.
